newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mekong region ministers seek private funding.
newsitem.headline: Mekong region ministers seek private funding.

text.p: Ministers of six countries through which the Mekong river flows on Friday called for more private sector funding for projects to harness the region's potential.

"While the donor community has been generous in supporting sub-regional projects, more support is needed," ministers from Burma, Cambodia, China, Laos, Thailand and Vietnam said in a joint statement at a meeting organised by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Manila.

The ADB is coordinating the efforts of the governments which want to build dams on the river and its tributaries for flood control, irrigation and the driving of turbines to generate electricity for the region's industrialising and urbanising economies.

"The GMS (Greater Mekong Subregion) initiatives will be half-complete if only the donor agencies are involved. From now on, we will see active participation from the private sector," ADB vice president Bong-Suh Lee told a news conference on the sidelines of the two-day meeting which ended on Friday.
Answering questions on the environmental impact of the projects, Lee said: "We are increasingly paying attention to the environment and social aspects of the projects."
An official statement said a Working Group on Environment (WGE) had met non-government organisations (NGOs) last month to discuss the issue.

At the ADB-hosted meeting, the ministers had agreed "on a plan of cooperation with the NGOs to address more effectively environmental and social aspects of development projects in the GMS," the statement said.
Lee said the Mekong sub-region required $13 billion to $15 billion to finance transport, telecommunications and energy projects in the next 10 years.
Of the 100 infrastructure projects identified, the private sector and multilateral financing institutions have committed to financing about 15 projects, he said.
